secrets.optionalReason: Found in the code; not needed to start the app.

deployNotes: Three pods, one service each: frontend (Nginx + React build), backend (Node/Socket.io) and db (PostgreSQL 15). The database is never co-located with the app.

The backend reaches the database at db.pod:5432. The Nginx config in the frontend must proxy /api and /socket.io (with WebSocket Upgrade headers) to backend.pod:<backendPort>, not to localhost or a bare hostname like 'backend'.
The backend port (5000 here) is inferred because the README is truncated. Confirm it against backend/Dockerfile or nexlayer.yaml and update the pod port and PORT env var to match.
The repo has its own Dockerfiles for each tier. Any database init SQL from database/ must be baked into the DB pod image or run by the backend on boot, since the pod uses a stock postgres image here.
Database credentials are generated by Nexlayer, so the placeholder password is only illustrative.
Socket.io needs WebSocket support through the proxy. If the backend is ever scaled to multiple replicas, it needs sticky sessions or a Redis adapter.

productionPlan.summary: Cat Chat runs as three services. The frontend serves the React build through Nginx and forwards /api and /socket.io (including WebSocket upgrades) to backend.pod:3001. The backend runs Express and Socket.io, and Postgres 15 is built from database/ with init.sql baked in. The most important production change is that the committed nexlayer.yaml contains a literal database password: it must come from the POSTGRES_PASSWORD key, and the database must keep its 2Gi volume so chat history survives restarts.

decisions.decision: Keep the existing three services: frontend (Nginx, port 80, public at /), backend (Node/Express/Socket.io, port 3001) and database (Postgres 15, port 5432). Each is built from its own folder and pushed as registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cat-chat-app-<service>:planned.
decisions.why: Each folder has its own Dockerfile, and nginx.conf already proxies to backend.pod:3001, which matches the backend service name and the port its Dockerfile exposes.

decisions.decision: Start from the existing nexlayer.yaml and change three things. Rename the app to cat-chat-app. Point the images at the planned registry paths. Replace both literal 'postgres' passwords (backend DB_PASSWORD and database POSTGRES_PASSWORD) with ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}, so both services resolve to one generated value.
decisions.why: The committed yaml exposes the database password in plain text, and the backend and database must share the same credential.

decisions.decision: Build Postgres from database/Dockerfile (postgres:15-alpine plus init.sql). Keep major version 15, user postgres and database catchat.
decisions.why: The repo pins Postgres 15, and the schema lives in database/init.sql, which only runs if it is baked into the image's docker-entrypoint-initdb.d.

decisions.decision: Keep the 2Gi volume postgres-data mounted at /var/lib/postgresql, with PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data.
decisions.why: Messages and users live in Postgres and must survive restarts. Mounting the parent folder avoids the lost+found folder that breaks initdb.

decisions.decision: Only the frontend is public, at path /. The browser reaches the backend through Nginx on the same origin. The backend reaches the database at database.pod:5432. CLIENT_URL is set to <% URL %> for Socket.io CORS.
decisions.why: server.js limits Socket.io CORS to CLIENT_URL (default http://localhost:3000), and nginx.conf already proxies /api/ and /socket.io/ with Upgrade headers.
server.js keeps online users and socket mappings in in-memory Maps (activeUsers, userSockets), so a second instance would split users and break presence and typing events.

decisions.decision: Use GET /api/health as the backend health check, reached publicly through the frontend proxy.
decisions.why: server.js defines /api/health and it returns {status:'ok'} without touching the database.

fix_before_production.title: Remove the literal database password from the committed nexlayer.yaml
fix_before_production.why: DB_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD are committed as 'postgres', which exposes the credential. Use ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} as in the planned yaml, and treat the old value as compromised.

fix_before_production.title: Drop the hardcoded POSTGRES_PASSWORD ENV from the database image
fix_before_production.why: The image bakes in a default password. If the runtime key were ever missing, the database would start with 'postgres' instead of failing.

fix_before_production.title: Make the frontend's API and Socket.io URLs same-origin in the production build
fix_before_production.why: The code reads REACT_APP_API_URL and REACT_APP_SOCKET_URL at build time. If they fall back to a localhost address, browsers cannot reach the backend; they should be empty or relative so traffic goes through the Nginx proxy.

verify_after_deploy: GET / on the app URL returns 200 with the React index.html
GET /api/health on the app URL returns 200 with {"status":"ok"}
GET /api/rooms on the app URL returns 200 JSON, not 500, proving the backend reached database.pod and init.sql created the schema
GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling on the app URL returns 200 with a Socket.io handshake payload
Send a message, restart the database service, then GET /api/messages and confirm the message is still returned
open_questions: The existing deployment is named 'cat-chat'; this plan deploys as 'cat-chat-app'. Does the old deployment's chat history need to be migrated, or is starting fresh acceptable?
Will the backend ever need more than one instance? That would require a shared Socket.io adapter (e.g. Redis) and moving the in-memory online-users state out of server.js.
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: cat-chat-app
  pods:
    # Frontend - React build served by Nginx, proxies /api and /socket.io to backend.pod:3001
    - name: frontend
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cat-chat-app-frontend:planned"
      path: /
      servicePorts:
        - 80

    # Backend - Node.js + Express + Socket.io (single instance: in-memory presence)
    - name: backend
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cat-chat-app-backend:planned"
      servicePorts:
        - 3001
      vars:
        NODE_ENV: production
        PORT: "3001"
        DB_HOST: database.pod
        DB_PORT: "5432"
        DB_NAME: catchat
        DB_USER: postgres
        DB_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
        CLIENT_URL: "<% URL %>"

    # Database - PostgreSQL 15 with init.sql baked in
    - name: database
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cat-chat-app-database:planned"
      servicePorts:
        - 5432
      vars:
        POSTGRES_DB: catchat
        POSTGRES_USER: postgres
        POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
        PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      volumes:
        - name: postgres-data
          size: 2Gi
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql
